es.summary: Los macrólidos son antibióticos que inhiben la síntesis proteica bacteriana y la enzima hepática CYP3A4, aumentando la concentración de fármacos metabolizados por esta vía.
key_points: Inhiben la subunidad 50S del ribosoma y la CYP3A4 hepática.
Usados para neumonía, infecciones respiratorias y de piel.
Pueden prolongar el QT y causar arritmias graves.
Interaccionan con estatinas, anticoagulantes y anticonceptivos hormonales.
Reacciones alérgicas graves y hepatotoxicidad son efectos serios.

mechanism: Se unen a la subunidad 50S del ribosoma e impiden la translocación del péptido.
Bloquean la síntesis de proteínas bacterianas, deteniendo el crecimiento.
Inhiben la enzima hepática CYP3A4, reduciendo el metabolismo de fármacos coadministrados.
Aumentan la concentración plasmática de medicamentos dependientes de CYP3A4.
indications: Infecciones de piel y tejidos blandos.
Profilaxis de infecciones en cirugía torácica.
contraindications: Historia de arritmia con QT prolongado.
Uso concomitante de antiarrítmicos que prolongan el QT (p. ej., sotalol).
adverse_effects: Prolongación del QT → torsades de pointes (serious).
interactions: Aumenta niveles de simvastatina → riesgo de miopatía.
Potencia efecto anticoagulante de warfarina → INR elevado.
Reduce la eficacia de anticonceptivos hormonales.
Incrementa niveles de ciclosporina y tacrolimus.
nursing_care: Verificar alergias a macrólidos antes de administrar.
Obtener ECG basal y monitorizar intervalo QT durante el tratamiento.
Controlar pruebas de función hepática al iniciar y durante la terapia.
Observar signos de arritmia: palpitaciones, síncope.
Retener la dosis si QT >500 ms o si aparecen reacciones alérgicas graves.
Notificar al médico ante cualquier alteración significativa.
patient_teaching: Tomar el medicamento según indicación, con o sin alimentos según prescripción.
Completar todo el ciclo aunque los síntomas mejoren.
Reportar palpitaciones, mareos o erupciones cutáneas inmediatamente.
Evitar iniciar nuevos medicamentos sin consultar al profesional de salud.
Usar método anticonceptivo adicional durante el tratamiento.

outcomes: Sin signos de hipersensibilidad durante 48 h del inicio del tratamiento
Mantener signos vitales dentro de rangos normales

interventions.action: Evaluar historial de alergias y reacciones previas a antibióticos antes de la administración.
interventions.rationale: Identificar pacientes con mayor probabilidad de reacción alérgica.

interventions.action: Obtener y monitorear ECG basal y cada 48 h para detectar prolongación del QT.
interventions.rationale: Prevenir arritmias graves asociadas a la inhibición de CYP3A4.

interventions.action: Vigilar signos vitales y síntomas de anafilaxia (urticaria, dificultad respiratoria).
interventions.rationale: Detectar rápidamente una reacción alérgica y actuar a tiempo.

interventions.action: Retener la dosis y notificar al médico si aparecen erupciones, prurito o dificultad para respirar.
interventions.rationale: Evitar progresión a una reacción alérgica severa.

interventions.action: Administrar oxígeno y preparar epinefrina 0.3 mg IM si se presenta anafilaxia.
interventions.rationale: Tratar emergencias alérgicas según protocolos de soporte vital.

en.summary: Macrolides are antibiotics that inhibit bacterial protein synthesis and the hepatic enzyme CYP3A4, increasing the concentration of drugs metabolized by this pathway.
key_points: Inhibit the 50S ribosomal subunit and hepatic CYP3A4.
Used for pneumonia, respiratory and skin infections.
Can prolong the QT interval and cause serious arrhythmias.
Interact with statins, anticoagulants and hormonal contraceptives.
Severe allergic reactions and hepatotoxicity are serious effects.

mechanism: Bind to the 50S ribosomal subunit and block peptide translocation.
Block bacterial protein synthesis, stopping growth.
Inhibit hepatic CYP3A4, reducing metabolism of coadministered drugs.
Increase plasma concentrations of CYP3A4-dependent medications.
indications: Prophylaxis of infections in thoracic surgery.
contraindications: Concurrent use of QT-prolonging antiarrhythmics (e.g., sotalol).
interactions: Increases simvastatin levels → risk of myopathy.
Potentiates warfarin anticoagulant effect → elevated INR.
Increases levels of cyclosporine and tacrolimus.
nursing_care: Check for macrolide allergies before administration.
Obtain baseline ECG and monitor QT interval during therapy.
Check liver function tests at initiation and during treatment.
Observe for arrhythmia signs: palpitations, syncope.
Hold dose if QT >500 ms or if severe allergic reactions occur.
Notify physician of any significant changes.
patient_teaching: Take medication as prescribed, with or without food as directed.
Complete the full course even if symptoms improve.
Report palpitations, dizziness, or skin rashes immediately.
Avoid starting new medications without consulting a health professional.
Use additional contraceptive method during treatment.

outcomes: No signs of hypersensitivity within 48 h of treatment start
Vital signs remain within normal ranges

interventions.action: Assess allergy history and prior antibiotic reactions before administration.
interventions.rationale: Identify patients at higher risk of allergic reaction.

interventions.action: Obtain and monitor baseline ECG and every 48 h to detect QT prolongation.
interventions.rationale: Prevent serious arrhythmias associated with CYP3A4 inhibition.

interventions.action: Monitor vital signs and anaphylaxis symptoms (hives, respiratory distress).
interventions.rationale: Rapidly detect an allergic reaction and act promptly.

interventions.action: Hold dose and notify physician if rashes, itching or breathing difficulty occur.
interventions.rationale: Prevent progression to severe allergic reaction.

interventions.action: Administer oxygen and prepare 0.3 mg IM epinephrine if anaphylaxis occurs.
interventions.rationale: Treat allergic emergencies per advanced life support protocols.

summary.0.quote: Macrolides inhibit the liver enzyme cytochrome P450 3A4 (CYP3A4), which is responsible for metabolizing many medications.

sections.mechanism.0.quote: When a penicillin is administered, the beta-lactam ring of penicillin will bind to the penicillin-binding protein and inhibit it.

sections.mechanism.1.quote: Oxazolidinones work by inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis to suppress further growth and multiplication of the bacteria.

sections.mechanism.2.quote: Macrolides inhibit the liver enzyme cytochrome P450 3A4 (CYP3A4), which is responsible for metabolizing many medications.

sections.indications.0.quote: Macrolide Azithromycin ( Zithromax ) Pneumonia, community acquired: Adults: 500 mg orally on day 1, then 250 mg once daily for 4 days.

sections.indications.1.quote: Because fluoroquinolones have been associated with serious adverse reactions, ciprofloxacin is reserved for use in clients who have no alternative treatment options for the following indications: acute exacerbation of chronic bronchitis, acute sinusitis, and acute uncomplicated cystitis.

sections.indications.2.quote: Cephalosporin Cephalexin ( Keflex ) Skin or soft tissue infection: Adults and children ≥15 years: 250 mg capsule orally every 6 hours or 500 mg orally every 12 hours for 7–14 days.

sections.indications.3.quote: Therefore, macrolides are useful for treating a variety of respiratory conditions, such as pneumonia and Legionnaires’ disease, as well as chlamydia, a sexually transmitted infection (STI).

sections.adverse_effects.0.quote: Most oral antibiotics can cause gastrointestinal discomfort, including nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea.

sections.adverse_effects.1.quote: Adverse Effects Headache Skin rash Abdominal pain Diarrhea Dizziness QT interval prolongation Contraindications Hypersensitivity Pregnancy Coadministration with QT interval–prolonging drugs

sections.adverse_effects.2.quote: Adverse Effects Headache Skin rash Abdominal pain Diarrhea Dizziness QT interval prolongation Contraindications Hypersensitivity Pregnancy Coadministration with QT interval–prolonging drugs

sections.adverse_effects.3.quote: Macrolides are also capable of inhibiting potassium efflux out of myocardial cells, leading to prolongation of the heart rate–corrected QT interval (QTc) on an electrocardiogram (ECG/EKG) and increasing the client’s risk for developing torsades de pointes, a potentially fatal ventricular dysrhythmia.

sections.nursing_care.1.quote: Monitor the ECG for prolongation of the QTc interval when clients are taking systemically acting agents.

sections.nursing_care.2.quote: Monitor liver function tests to assess for liver injury.

sections.nursing_care.5.quote: Notify prescriber if blood counts drop.

sections.patient_teaching.1.quote: Take the entire course of antibiotics, even if they begin to feel better.

sections.patient_teaching.3.quote: Alert their health care provider about starting any new medications that may interact with their antifungal therapy.
